sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: After a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, defender Lisandro Martinez publicly criticised Manchester United's hierarchy for insufficient investment in the squad. He specifically questioned the technical director, Jason Wilcox, and suggested the club failed to build a strong enough team following their Champions League qualification. The club has struggled recently, failing to win in five matches.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The comments have sparked debate regarding player conduct and club management. Former players Wayne Rooney and Ashley Young argued the public criticism was disrespectful to teammates and could harm dressing room morale. Conversely, some observers and fans feel Martinez's honesty reflects long-standing concerns about recruitment and ownership decisions under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Omar Berrada.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Manager Michael Carrick, who has not yet seen the full interview, indicated he would address the matter after gathering more information. The club faces ongoing pressure regarding its recruitment strategy, financial debt, and the performance of the current squad.
